svg.text: DDIA 12 · THE FUTURE OF DATA SYSTEMS
The book's conclusion: there is no one database that does everything. Build systems as a source of truth plus derived views connected by logs.
Every other store is a derived view, like an index or
materialized view, except in separate specialized systems. Any
view can be dropped and rebuilt by replaying the log.
Kappa: one stream path, reprocess by replay
Kappa: one streaming codebase. To fix a bug or change logic,
start v2 reading the log from the beginning, let it catch up,
The duplicate hits the unique constraint, and the server
returns the original result. Only an end-to-end ID from the
"How do you guarantee no double charge?"
Client idempotency key + unique constraint + the payment provider's idempotency + a daily reconciliation job
"Search is a derived view. Timeliness can lag seconds; the checkout price is read from the source of truth
"How would you change the aggregation logic?"
Kappa: deploy v2 consumer from offset 0 to a new table, compare, switch.
"I separate integrity from timeliness: money and inventory are strongly consistent and audited;
everything the user browses is a derived, eventually consistent view."
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.
